slides.title: Network Security Basics
content: Network security is the practice of protecting network systems, data, and devices from unauthorized access, attacks, and misuse
It ensures confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA triad) of data during transmission and storage
It prevents threats like malware, phishing, denial-of-service attacks, and unauthorized access
It uses technologies like firewalls, encryption, VPNs, and intrusion detection systems to secure networks

slides.title: Core Security Principles
content: Confidentiality ensures that sensitive data is accessible only to authorized users using encryption techniques
Integrity ensures that data is not altered during transmission using hashing and checksums
Availability ensures that network resources are accessible to authorized users when needed
Authentication and authorization verify user identity and control access to resources, while accountability tracks user actions

slides.title: Firewalls
content: A firewall is a security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predefined rules
It acts as a barrier between trusted internal networks and untrusted external networks like the internet
It protects against unauthorized access, cyberattacks, and malicious traffic
Firewalls can be implemented as hardware, software, or a combination of both

slides.title: Types of Firewalls
content: Packet filtering firewalls operate at the network layer and inspect packet headers like IP addresses, ports, and protocols using static rules
Stateful inspection firewalls operate at the transport layer and track active connections using a state table for dynamic filtering
Packet filtering is simple and fast but less secure, while stateful inspection provides better security but requires more resources
Advanced firewalls like application layer firewalls perform deep packet inspection to detect complex threats

slides.title: TLS and SSL
content: TLS (Transport Layer Security) and SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) are cryptographic protocols used to secure communication over networks
They provide confidentiality through encryption, integrity through hashing, and authentication using digital certificates
TLS is the modern and secure successor of SSL, widely used in HTTPS, email security, and VPNs
They use public key infrastructure (PKI) to verify identities and establish secure communication channels

slides.title: TLS/SSL Working
content: The TLS/SSL process begins with a handshake where client and server agree on encryption methods and exchange keys
The server provides a digital certificate to verify its identity using a trusted certificate authority
A session key is generated using asymmetric encryption and used for encrypting data using symmetric encryption
All transmitted data is encrypted and decrypted securely, ensuring protection from eavesdropping and tampering
